components.css: .ds-route { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 28px; margin: 0; padding: 0; color: #fff; font-family: Poppins, 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, Geneva, Verdana, sans-serif; list-style: none; } .ds-route::before { position: absolute; top: 22px; right: calc(33.333% - 23px); left: 23px; height: 1px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(132,190,195,0.8) 0 7px, transparent 7px 13px); content: ''; } .ds-route-stop { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 46px minmax(0,1fr); gap: 13px; min-width: 0; } .ds-route-marker { position: relative; z-index: 1; display: grid; width: 46px; height: 46px; place-items: center; border: 1px solid #79aeb4; border-radius: 50%; background: #082038; color: #bfe4e2; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 800; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-route-origin .ds-route-marker { border-color: #ffd35a; background: #ffd35a; color: #082038; } .ds-route-stop strong { display: block; color: #fff; font-size: 0.94rem; } .ds-route-stop p { max-width: 30ch; margin: 5px 0 0; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.68); font-size: 0.78rem; line-height: 1.5; } @media (max-width: 700px) { .ds-route { grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr); gap: 20px; } .ds-route::before { top: 22px; bottom: 22px; left: 22px; width: 1px; height: auto; background: repeating-linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(132,190,195,0.8) 0 7px, transparent 7px 13px); } }

narrative.overview:
AssistDesk keeps its established campus-helpdesk identity—navy, teal, white, and gold—while giving the support journey a distinct, reusable wayfinding language. A fine map grid, connected numbered stops, and restrained destination markers make the route legible; clear type and direct labels remain the primary information layer.

The Campus Wayfinding Board direction was inferred as the assigned lead after the decision page closed without a stored answer and confirmation returned no selection; it was not a recorded user selection. The implemented surface pairs a dark route field with a quiet directory and a pale closing panel, keeping the existing AssistDesk identity recognizable while making the request-to-department-to-status sequence easy to scan.
keyCharacteristics: Campus support expressed as a clear, connected route.
Navy-led contrast with teal route details and signal-gold actions.
Information stays readable and explicit; map graphics support rather than replace it.

rules.name: The Gold Signal Rule
rules.body: Reserve the brighter signal gold for the primary action and the route origin; do not treat it as a broad decorative fill.

rules.name: The Clear-Label Rule
rules.body: Keep meaningful route steps and actions in text; condensed numbering and graphic marks are supporting wayfinding, not substitutes for labels.

rules.name: The Route-Orientation Rule
rules.body: Preserve the same ordered three-stop path across breakpoints: horizontal on wide screens and vertical on narrow screens.

dos: Do keep the inherited navy/teal/gold identity and use the brighter signal gold for the principal action and route origin.
Do use connected route lines and numbered destination markers to clarify an explicitly labeled support sequence.
Do preserve the 1216px content measure and the horizontal-to-vertical route transformation.
Do keep keyboard focus visible and honor reduced-motion preferences for interactive transitions.
donts: Don't let map graphics replace labels, controls, or readable explanations.
Don't add unsupported response-time promises, service counts, guarantees, or customer claims.
Don't turn the flat route and directory into a stack of shadowed cards.
